notes: Novel story — Live Preview does not exist in the codebase. The attachment point is the page-level provider that feeds all 28+ useContent consumers. VCs derived solely from description since ACs are empty. All Contentstack-external criteria are written to our side of the boundary with explicit mock assumptions.

notes: Openspec produced empty acceptance criteria, so all 15 ACs are newly derived from the story title ('Live Preview of Content in CMS'), the three brands (GO/UP/MX), the catch-all page route, and the noted 28+ useContent consumers. Key areas covered: (1) AC-1/AC-3 define preview vs. production mode activation and isolation; (2) AC-2/AC-9/AC-12/AC-13 cover content propagation including nested content, structural changes, and rapid updates; (3) AC-4/AC-5/AC-14 address error handling for disconnections, reconnections, and API errors; (4) AC-6 addresses security against spoofed preview parameters; (5) AC-7 covers accessibility of dynamic updates; (6) AC-8 ensures the catch-all route works at any depth; (7) AC-10 ensures all three brands are supported; (8) AC-11 guarantees zero performance overhead outside preview mode; (9) AC-15 covers entry navigation within the CMS. CAVEAT: Without reading the actual file contents (especially [[...slug]].tsx and the mock/interface files), I am inferring the architecture. If the actual implementation uses a different data-fetching pattern than assumed (e.g., getStaticProps vs. server-side rendering vs. client-side), some ACs may need adjustment. Specifically, AC-11 (zero bundle overhead) may need revision if Contentstack's live preview SDK requires client-side inclusion — in that case it should be changed to 'no measurable overhead to runtime performance when not in preview mode, and any preview-only code is lazy-loaded.'
